answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The harbor multiplier is published, charged in timber, and juniper lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4212 identities would post 3082 proofs and burn roughly 22 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
